headline: Attruby growth narrows losses ahead of three drug launches

kpis.label: Net loss attributable to common stockholders
Net loss attributable to common stockholders

summary_short: BridgeBio's Q2 2026 revenue grew 120.4% y/y to $243.7M, driven by $222.4M of Attruby net product sales. The net loss to common stockholders narrowed to $152.2M (-$0.78/share) from $181.9M a year ago, as a $1 billion preferred equity raise closed July 1, 2026 to fund three pending drug launches.
summary_long: Revenue of $243.7M (+120.4% y/y, +25.3% q/q) was driven by a $150.9M y/y rise in Attruby net product sales and $13.8M more royalty revenue, partly offset by lower license revenue after a 2025 one-time $30.0M milestone. Total operating costs rose $106.0M y/y to $350.8M on higher SG&A ($57.1M) and R&D ($38.2M), but revenue growth outpaced it, narrowing the operating loss to $107.1M from $134.3M and net loss to common stockholders to $152.2M from $181.9M. Cash and equivalents fell to $677.9M on operating burn and a $210.0M buyback; broader cash-plus-securities rose to $720.2M on 2033 Notes proceeds. No numeric guidance was issued; a $1B preferred equity raise closed July 1, 2026 funding three pending FDA drug launches.

drivers.explanation: CEO Neil Kumar cited growing evidence of Attruby's kidney-protective profile, all three pipeline programs (BBP-418, encaleret, infigratinib) moving into active FDA review, and the $1B preferred equity raise sizing the balance sheet to fund all three launches.

Growth was driven by a $150.9M y/y increase in Attruby net product revenue and a $13.8M royalty increase from BEYONTTRA sales in the EU and Japan, partly offset by lower license/services revenue after a $30.0M one-time 2025 milestone.
The $11.4M y/y increase in cost of revenues was primarily due to higher sales volume of Attruby.
The y/y operating loss narrowed because $133.1M of revenue growth outpaced the $106.0M rise in operating costs (SG&A +$57.1M for commercial/launch prep, R&D +$38.2M for late-stage programs).

drivers.metric: Net loss attributable to common stockholders
drivers.explanation: Narrower operating loss drove most of the y/y improvement, partly offset by a $15.3M increase in noncash interest expense on deferred royalty obligations.
Per-share loss narrowed 17.9% y/y, more than the 16.3% narrowing in aggregate net loss, since the smaller dollar loss was spread over only 2.8% more diluted shares.

Cash and equivalents alone fell on $268.4M of operating cash used in H1 and a $210.0M share buyback; the broader cash-plus-marketable-securities figure the release highlights rose to $720.2M on 2033 Notes proceeds.
The stockholders' deficit widened as accumulated net losses continue to exceed contributed capital; the release does not separately explain the equity-deficit trend.

No numeric FY2026 or Q3 2026 guidance (revenue, EPS, capex, or expense ranges) was disclosed in this release — only qualitative pipeline-timing statements (PDUFA dates, launch timing) — so guidance[] on the shard was left untouched.
